claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy fabricated as a nanoscale thin film or lithographically patterned nanoribbon.
Substrate mismatch can controllably introduce lattice strain into the target material.
Lithographic patterning can controllably introduce lattice strain into the target material.
Introduced lattice strain changes magnetic anisotropy in the target FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Introduced lattice strain changes magnetic domain structure in the target FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Magnetic nanodomain structure can influence magnetic softness and hysteresis-related behavior in high-entropy alloys.
Strain-induced changes in magnetic anisotropy and domain structure enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Strain-induced changes in magnetic anisotropy and domain structure reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed strain-mediated effects apply near room temperature, at low applied magnetic fields, and in nanoscale geometries.
The as-deposited comparison baseline can be treated as being without lattice strain.
The magnitude of the predicted enhancement and hysteresis reduction, and the optimal strain conditions, are unknown.
The hypothesis can be tested by varying introduced strain and measuring magnetocaloric response and hysteresis against the as-deposited baseline.
No significant change in either magnetocaloric response or hysteresis upon introducing strain would falsify the hypothesis.
